reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.74.1-Ps.74.3 re-derived independently. Numbering first: web_mt_offset_map.json gives Ps 74 rule 'identity' (web_verses 23 / mt_verses 23, web_title true, mt_title_verses empty, note 'identity_confirmed_by_kjv_note_on_v1'), so WEB and MT verse numbers coincide in this span (23 verses / 23 verses) and the title pseudo-ref web:Ps.74.0 = oshb:Ps.74.1 is the owner-ruled form for a titled opening row — correct as written. The superscription claim holds at byte level: MT 74:1 opens on the two title tokens מַשְׂכִּ֗יל לְאָ֫סָ֥ף (words 1-2 of 10), and psalm_device_inventory.json superscriptions/74 lists exactly labels maskil + le_asaph. The device_notes figures re-derive exactly from genre_label_membership: maskil = 13 psalms [32,42,44,45,52,53,54,55,74,78,88,89,142], le_asaph = 12 psalms [50,73-83] (unit: psalms, book-wide) — the row's '13 and 12 psalms book-wide' is right. All 3 Hebrew quotes collate at BYTE tier against their cited refs (collate.py): לָמָ֣ה at oshb:Ps.74.1 (word 3 of 10, i.e. the first word after the superscription — the row's 'opens the lament' is the precise formulation, not 'opens the verse'), זְכֹ֤ר at oshb:Ps.74.2 (word 1 of 12) and הָרִ֣ימָה at oshb:Ps.74.3 (word 1 of 8). The twin-imperative warrant is sound on the bytes plus both witnesses: 74:2 and 74:3 each open on a prefix-less volitive with the 2ms addressee sustained from 74:1, and WEB reads “Remember your congregation, which you purchased of old,” (web:Ps.74.2) and “Lift up your feet to the perpetual ruins,” (web:Ps.74.3). The closing seam is the 1 candidate of the 2 in reach that carries a discourse shift: 74:4 opens on שָׁאֲג֣וּ with the subject צֹ֭רְרֶיךָ following, turning 2ms address into third-person report of the adversaries' acts, while the rival seam at 74:2|74:3 has 0 shifts to stand on (2 verses, 2 imperative openings), so the row took the better tier-1 warrant. Disclosure objects check out: pmarks_Ps.json records 0 selah verses in Ps 74 of 71 book-wide (unit: verses) and the row cites 0; paseq sits at Ps.74.2 (2 segs) but is seg-layer and uncited, correctly; pe/samekh claims number 0, the layer being absent book-wide. Two observations, neither filed. (1) device_notes says the psalm 'continues the Asaph collection opened at Psalm 73'; the le_asaph membership is [50, 73-83], so the contiguous Book III run of 11 psalms opens at 73 while the twelfth, Ps 50, stands apart in Book II — true as written under the ordinary reading of 'collection', but the 12-count sits close enough to invite mis-pairing. (2) Cluster-wide quote-convention drift, noted once here rather than filed five times: glosses of Hebrew tokens are set in curly double quotes in some slots and curly singles in others within one sentence, and the curly-double glosses include at least 1 that is not WEB-verbatim in case. The book-wide convention reserves curly doubles for WEB text; check_web_quotes.py cannot catch it here because these glosses sit beside oshb: refs rather than web: refs. Content is accurate where re-derived; this is an author-wave normalization, not a defect in the decision.

Span Ps.74.4-Ps.74.8. The core warrant survives re-derivation: שָׁאֲג֣וּ collates BYTE at oshb:Ps.74.4 (word 1 of 7) and the opening person shift away from the 2ms petition of 1-3 is real, as is the shift at the far seam, where אֽוֹתֹתֵ֗ינוּ and רָ֫אִ֥ינוּ at oshb:Ps.74.9 (both BYTE) carry 1st-plural reference. Both WEB quotes are verbatim (check_web_quotes.py, 0 flags across the cluster's 11 quotes). K/Q handling is correct by omission: pmarks_Ps.json records a ketiv/qere at MT 74:6 — inside this row's span — but the row quotes 0 Hebrew tokens from 74:6, and disclosure is owed when quoted. check_refs_mirror.py is GREEN: 74:9 is argued outside the span and does appear in boundary_evidence_refs. Two defects nonetheless. First and more serious, the row leaves a byte-true lexical link straddling its own 8|9 seam undisclosed, which under the standing cross-seam rule argues continuity against the split it makes. Second, the grammatical labels the row uses to justify that same seam are wrong on the bytes: the qatal plural is gender-unmarked, and the 4-8 block is not uniformly plural in any case. Neither defect moves the seam in my judgement — the 1st-plural turn at 74:9 is a genuine tier-1 signal — but both are material to the evidence set that seam rests on, and the first must be cured as one edit installed on this row and on the 74:9 row together.

challenges.claim: The row closes at 74:8 without disclosing that the 'signs' noun standing twice inside its own span at MT 74:4 is the contrastive partner of the very head-word the next row opens on at MT 74:9 — a byte-true lexical link straddling this row's 8|9 seam, which the standing cross-seam rule requires be disclosed and answered rather than passed over.
challenges.evidence: Tokens spliced from verse_map_oshb.json and collated with collate.py, all BYTE tier: oshb:Ps.74.4 word 6 of 7 אוֹתֹתָ֣ם and word 7 of 7 אֹתֽוֹת; oshb:Ps.74.9 word 1 of 11 אֽוֹתֹתֵ֗ינוּ. Sweep, object named FIRST = the noun's attested spellings, swept separately because the two 74:4 tokens differ in plene/defective spelling and a single skeleton query cannot cover both (unit: verses, MT-keyed, scope Ps 74): skeleton of the 74:4 word-6 spelling = 1 verse (74:4); skeleton of the 74:4 word-7 spelling = 1 verse (74:4); skeleton of the 74:9 word-1 spelling = 1 verse (74:9). Total 3 tokens over 2 verses, and those 2 verses sit on opposite sides of this row's closing seam. The link is visible in the English witness too: “They have set up their standards as signs.” (web:Ps.74.4) against “We see no miraculous signs.” (web:Ps.74.9) — WEB renders both with 'signs'. The suffix contrast (their / our) is carried in the pointed bytes of the two tokens above. The row cites oshb:Ps.74.9 in boundary_evidence_refs (1 of the row's 2 refs) and argues it as a person shift; the noun appears in 0 of the row's 3 observed_substrate_signals, which name 74:4's opening verb and 74:8's burning. Standing rule (Esth lesson d): a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed. Cure is one authored disclosure installed on both seam rows in the same pass (Job lesson a); filed as the paired entry OL-223-2 on the 74:9-74:11 row.

challenges.claim: The row labels the 74:4 verb a '3mp verb' and the 4-8 block a '3mp narrative'; the suffix-conjugation plural is gender-unmarked on the bytes, and the block is not uniformly plural, so the label asserts a distinction the forms do not carry and mischaracterises the span it is used to delimit.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.74.4 word 1 of 7 שָׁאֲג֣וּ (collate.py: BYTE) ends in the plural vocalic affix shared by masculine and feminine subjects in the suffix conjugation; nothing in the pointed bytes marks gender. The row's own parallel label proves it knows the convention: it tags oshb:Ps.74.9 word 3 of 11 רָ֫אִ֥ינוּ (collate.py: BYTE), the same conjugation in the 1st person, as '1cp' — common gender — while tagging the 3rd-person plural as '3mp' in the same sentence of rejected_alternative. The block-level characterisation also fails inside the span: oshb:Ps.74.5 opens on יִ֭וָּדַע (collate.py: BYTE), a prefix-conjugation form carrying no plural affix, 1 of the 8 finite forms in the span. Census (object: finite verb forms, unit: forms, scope 74:4-74:8, read off the pointed bytes): 6 suffix-conjugation plural forms, at 74:4 words 1 and 5, 74:7 words 1 and 5, 74:8 words 1 and 5 — 6 of 6 carrying the gender-neutral vocalic plural affix; 1 prefix-conjugation plural, at 74:6 word 7, which is the one form in the span whose conjugation does mark gender; and 1 prefix-conjugation singular, 74:5 word 1. So the span the row calls a '3mp narrative' runs on a conjugation that cannot show gender, and is not uniformly plural either. WEB masks the difference by rendering 74:5 “They behaved like men wielding axes, cutting through a thicket of trees.” (web:Ps.74.5), so the English cannot be used to rescue the label. TOOLKIT.md records that no morphology layer is staged, so form claims must be argued from the pointed bytes — argued that way, 'third-person plural' is supportable and '3mp' is not.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.74.9-Ps.74.11. The segmentation is well warranted and I do not contest it: אֽוֹתֹתֵ֗ינוּ opens 74:9 (BYTE at oshb:Ps.74.9), the interrogatives עַד מָתַ֣י at oshb:Ps.74.10 (words 1-2 of 9, BYTE) and לָ֤מָּה at oshb:Ps.74.11 (word 1 of 8, BYTE) are byte-true as cited, and the far seam is strong — 74:12 opens the hymnic pivot. The device_notes sweep re-derives exactly: the interrogative's skeleton spelling hits 2 verses in Ps 74, 74:1 and 74:11 (unit: verses, scope Ps 74; book-wide control for the same skeleton is 24 verses, so the enumerated refs are what pin the scope here). I considered and did NOT file two things. (a) citation_sweep.py emits one WARN — the Hebrew quote in observed_substrate_signals[1] binds to K/Q verse oshb:Ps.74.11 with no ketiv/qere disclosure in-field. The row does disclose the pair twice elsewhere (rationale, and observed_substrate_signals[2]) and carries 'oshb:Ps.74.11 (ketiv/qere)' in boundary_evidence_refs, which is the prescribed parenthetical exception; on the settled scope analogue for dual-cites, satisfaction at the refs array is compliance and in-field repetition is an author-wave enhancement, so this is a WARN, not a defect. (b) The device_notes phrase 'the interrogative lamah that opens the psalm' — in MT the token is word 3 of 74:1, behind the two-word superscription — is ordinary usage for a psalm body and the sibling row states it precisely. What I do file is a quotation-grade failure on the one pointed token the row reproduces from the K/Q pair, and the shared seam defect carried over from the 74:4-74:8 row.

challenges.claim: The pointed qere token the row reproduces for the MT 74:11 ketiv/qere pair is not byte-true against the source: it collates at nfd tier, which is not quotation-grade for pointed text, and the row presents it without any tier label — a live instance of the copy-degradation hazard, inside the very parenthetical that exists to disclose the K/Q pair.
challenges.evidence: collate.py against oshb:Ps.74.11 returns tier=nfd for the row's qere token חֵֽיקְךָ֣ and tier=byte for its ketiv token חוקך. Codepoints, row token: U+05D7 U+05B5 U+05BD U+05D9 U+05E7 U+05B0 U+05DA U+05B8 U+05A3. Codepoints, source token spliced from verse_map_oshb.json (oshb:Ps.74.11 word 7 of 8): U+05D7 U+05BD U+05B5 U+05D9 U+05E7 U+05B0 U+05DA U+05B8 U+05A3. Same codepoint set, different combining order — the source orders meteg U+05BD before tsere U+05B5 and the row inverts the pair; NFD-normalised the two are equal, byte-wise they are not. Byte proof over the frozen file, so this is not shell transit on my side: the HET+TSERE+METEG byte sequence occurs 1 time in freeze/rows_v0.jsonl and 0 times in the source order, while verse_map_oshb.json holds HET+METEG+TSERE exactly once, at this token. TOOLKIT.md is explicit that only byte tier is quotation-grade for pointed text and that 'nfd' means the bytes must be re-spliced from source; the cure is normalize_hebrew_in_json.py --write, not a retype. Note the checker does not catch this: citation_sweep.py accepts tier in ('byte','nfd') for pointed runs at line 312, so its GREEN does not certify byte tier. The ketiv token is byte-true because it is inline in the verse itself — חוקך stands unpointed at word 6 of 8 immediately before the pointed qere, the inline-ketiv configuration TOOLKIT.md flags for slicing and counting hazards.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.74.12-Ps.74.17. Both seams and the anaphora count survive re-derivation. וֵ֭אלֹהִים collates BYTE at oshb:Ps.74.12 (word 1 of 7) and אַתָּ֤ה BYTE at oshb:Ps.74.13 (word 1 of 9); WEB agrees with the pivot reading at “Yet God is my King of old, working salvation throughout the earth.” (web:Ps.74.12), and the far seam is the imperative return at oshb:Ps.74.18 word 1 of 9, זְכָר (BYTE). The sweep figure the row cites is correct: the pronoun's skeleton spelling hits 5 verses in Ps 74, 74:13-74:17, with 7 skeleton occurrences (unit: verses and occurrences respectively, scope Ps 74; book-wide control 116 verses). Every one of the 5 verses carries a genuine pronoun token rather than a substring artefact — checked per verse against the pointed bytes. I hold the span. What fails is one universal in the rationale: the distribution claim overstates what the same sweep shows, and the row's own device_notes states the correct version, so the row contradicts itself on the point. That makes it a precision defect in the warrant, not a boundary error — hence low severity, and the cure is a one-clause rewrite that the device_notes formulation already supplies.

challenges.claim: The rationale's universal that the recital 'opens each following clause' on the emphatic pronoun is falsified by the bytes: the pronoun is verse-initial in 4 of the 5 verses, not 5, and 3 further cola inside the recital open on other words, so an anaphora that is real but partial is stated as exceptionless.
challenges.evidence: Token positions re-derived from verse_map_oshb.json (object: the pronoun's skeleton spelling, sliced from oshb:Ps.74.13 word 1; unit: word position within the MT verse, scope 74:13-74:17): 74:13 word 1 of 9; 74:14 word 1 of 8; 74:15 words 1 and 5 of 8; 74:16 word 6 of 9; 74:17 words 1 and 8 of 9. Verse-initial in 4 verses of 5. The exception is oshb:Ps.74.16, which opens on לְךָ֣ (collate.py: BYTE) with the pronoun held back to word 6 — and WEB reproduces exactly that inversion: “The day is yours, the night is also yours. You have prepared the light and the sun.” (web:Ps.74.16), which is the chiastic verse of the recital, not an anaphoric one. At clause level the universal fails at 3 further cola: oshb:Ps.74.13 word 5 שִׁבַּ֖רְתָּ, oshb:Ps.74.14 word 5 תִּתְּנֶ֥נּוּ and oshb:Ps.74.17 word 6 קַ֥יִץ head cola carrying 0 pronoun tokens (3 colon-heads, 3 of 3 collating BYTE at their verses). The row's device_notes carries the accurate formulation — 'opens or reinforces the clause in 5 verses' — so the repair is to import that wording into the rationale; the 5-verse sweep figure itself needs no change.

reviews.reasoning: Span Ps.74.18-Ps.74.23, the psalm-final row. The span itself is right and tiles the psalm exactly (check_tiling.py over Ps.74.1-Ps.74.23: 23 verses expected, 23 covered, 5 decisions, no gaps or overlaps). All four Hebrew quotes are byte-true: זְכָר at oshb:Ps.74.18 word 1 of 9, קוּמָ֣ה at oshb:Ps.74.22 word 1 of 10, and זְכֹ֥ר at oshb:Ps.74.22 word 5 of 10 (collate.py, BYTE each). The three WEB quotes are verbatim, and 74:2 is argued outside the span and correctly carried in boundary_evidence_refs. The rejected_alternative is 1 sentence and carries its rival. pmarks_Ps.json records 0 selah verses in Ps 74 of 71 book-wide (unit: verses) and the row cites 0; the paseq at MT 74:18 is seg-layer and correctly left uncited. My challenges are both in the disclosure fields rather than the boundary: device_notes asserts a verse-opening distribution the bytes contradict at 74:22 — and contradicts this row's own rationale, which states the relation correctly — and the closing sentence carries a bare closure universal that the machine check flags. The span stands; the frame claim needs re-cutting.

challenges.claim: device_notes states that the 'remember' imperative 'opens 3 verses of this psalm (74:2, 74:18, 74:22)'; at MT 74:22 the token stands at word 5 of 10, so the verb opens 2 verses, not 3 — the sweep counted verses containing the form while the sentence predicates verse-initial position of the count, which is the count-object mismatch the standing discipline forbids.
challenges.evidence: Re-derived from verse_map_oshb.json (object named FIRST: the skeleton spelling of the imperative, sliced from oshb:Ps.74.2 word 1; unit: verses, scope Ps 74): 3 verses carry the skeleton — 74:2, 74:18, 74:22 — so the 3-verse sweep figure is itself correct. Verse-initial position, however, holds at only 2 of the 3: oshb:Ps.74.2 word 1 of 12 זְכֹ֤ר and oshb:Ps.74.18 word 1 of 9 זְכָר (both BYTE). MT 74:22 opens instead on קוּמָ֣ה (word 1 of 10, BYTE), with אֱ֭לֹהִים, רִיבָ֣ה and רִיבֶ֑ךָ intervening before the imperative זְכֹ֥ר at word 5 of 10 (BYTE). Both witnesses agree: “Arise, God! Plead your own cause. Remember how the foolish man mocks you all day.” (web:Ps.74.22) puts the arise-imperative first. The row's own rationale states the relation accurately — it has the imperative recurring at 74:22 alongside the arise-verb, not opening it — so device_notes contradicts the row it annotates, and the framing argument built on it (an opening-petition frame returning here) is overstated by one member. Scope also wants naming: the same skeleton runs to 54 verses book-wide (unit: verses), and only the enumerated refs mark the citation as psalm-scoped.

challenges.claim: The rationale closes on 'No further verse follows', a bare closure universal with no digit-bearing count beside it, which the widened universals lexicon requires and the machine check flags.
challenges.evidence: check_universals.py over the frozen row returns 1 flag of 3 claims seen: path [4].rationale, claim 'No further verse follows', context ending '…(web:Ps.74.23) No further verse follows.' The 1 digit adjacent is the verse number inside the ref, which is tier-4 metadata and cannot discharge a sweep obligation. The claim is true and cheaply re-derivable — web_mt_offset_map.json records Ps 74 as web_verses 23 / mt_verses 23 under rule 'identity', and verse_map_web.json carries no Ps.74.24 — so the cure is to carry the count (23 verses in both witnesses, unit: verses) rather than to drop the sentence. Filed low because the underlying fact is sound and the defect is the missing digit, not the assertion.
